issues.description: Field mismatch: Animal.name. The problem statement (task description) explicitly requires the Animal.name attribute to use java.lang.StringBuilder for efficient in-place modifications. The provided solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the field as a java.lang.String (private String name). This divergence can confuse students about the expected field type and the correct getter/setter semantics (whether they should expose a StringBuilder or a String), and may cause mismatches with tests or with instructions that assume StringBuilder usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the specification or clarify the spec. Recommended fix to align with the problem statement: change the Animal.name field type to StringBuilder (private StringBuilder name;), update the constructor to initialize it (this.name = new StringBuilder(name);), and adapt accessors. To preserve a simple API for other classes/tests, provide getName() that returns name.toString() and setName(String newName) that sets name.replace(0, name.length(), newName) (or accept a StringBuilder setter if intended). Update all usages in other classes (Seal, Pig, Goat, Farm, and any tests) to call getName() (String) or the chosen new accessor. Alternatively, if the solution intentionally prefers String, update the problem statement to remove the StringBuilder requirement and state that name is a String so students are not confused.

issues.description: Concept: the Animal.name attribute type. The problem statement text (instruction) explicitly tells students to use a StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute (to enable efficient name modifications). The UML diagram in the problem statement shows the attribute as name: String. The provided reference implementation (solution) implements Animal with a private String name and getName()/setName() that use String. This mismatch (StringBuilder vs String in the text vs UML vs solution) creates ambiguity about the intended type for the Animal.name attribute and whether constructors/getters/setters and usage (concatenation in messages) should accept/return StringBuilder or String. Students may implement the attribute differently from the tests/reference or be uncertain which artifact to follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation so all artifacts agree on the Animal.name type. Two viable options: (A) Prefer String (simpler): update the problem statement text and the UML to specify name: String and remove the StringBuilder recommendation; ensure any example concatenations assume getName() returns String. OR (B) Prefer StringBuilder: change the reference solution and template to declare the field as private StringBuilder name, update the constructor to accept StringBuilder (or accept String and wrap it), change getName()/setName() signatures/behaviour accordingly (e.g., getName(): StringBuilder or provide getNameString()), and update all call sites (message strings) to use name.toString() when concatenating. State the chosen option explicitly in the problem statement and update UML and template files to match.
